A session's writes are refused: (1) a line of next that opens with no `<actor>:` (right: `my-x: open the PR`, or an outside party, `Acme support: reply on the invoice`; `Status:` and `Note:` are no actor, `my-x:do` with no space after the colon is refused); (2) on an update, an open step reworded in next alone (its text with words added, the old step left unmarked): keep the step as it is, mark it done=[n] when the work is finished, or write a different action as a new line (a step marked dropped=[n] may be replaced by a longer one); progress goes on the project page, never in a step (to give an open step other words, pass reword={n: "<new text>"}); (3) a write that leaves an item that stays open with no open step in next: name who takes the next step, keep one open step (a held item's is the one its wake leads to), or close the item with complete, which is exempt; the owner's server-made step counts. A step with a commit id, a test count, a merged, live or deployed status or a "since 09:30" stamp is written all the same and the reply notes it. A line of next is refused unless it is <= 200 characters after its `<actor>: ` prefix, and <= 280 in all (a link counts by its text); only the text you write in a call is checked. Each line remembers the session whose write put it there, and a later update changes only its own sender's lines. A command the owner runs goes in a next line that starts `the owner:`, whole in backticks, never in the description or in the step (step=…: a one-line summary, see step below); his item page shows it in Your step as its own block with a copy button. A next line that starts `the owner:` and asks him to run something (an imperative run cue such as run, type, execute, enter, or a place phrase such as "In a terminal:"; a line where someone else runs it, "say go and I will run …", is not a cue) gets the command check on create and update, refused as `next line: …`, and only for the lines the call sets: the command goes in backticks or a fence. A line that only mentions a command, and lines for other sessions, are not checked. A `! ` line (a command typed into a pane) in a line that starts `the owner:`, bare, in backticks or after a colon or a run cue ("type ! cmd"), is refused whether or not the line asks him to run it: put the command in backticks; "done!" is not a `! ` line. A first line of next that starts `the owner:` (or `you:`, "the owner to …") on an item that is doing, blocked or verifying is refused when the call sets next, needs or the step: set step=<his step in one line>, or needs=decision with an ask (a create has no step). A next line that defers on another item in words (once, after, when, until or before, then a board#N; the words of [keywords.model_guards] defer_after_id also count) is refused unless after=["board#N"] names that item in the same item, since a wait written only in words wakes nobody when the item closes; give the wait its end too, ask_by=YYYY-MM-DD, the day it comes back to someone if board#N is still open (supplies=<what that item's output gives this one>). Right: next="my-x: ship the export once board#N closes", after=["board#N"], ask_by="2099-03-02". Only the lines the call sets are checked; a line that only mentions an item ("see board#N") is not a deferral; on an item waiting on his call (needs=decision) write "see board#N", not after=; wake=YYYY-MM-DD is the way to be reminded on a day. Links sit on the words (`blocked on [#7](url)`), never a naked URL or a bare id: a naked http(s) URL in description, next or ask is refused, write `[words](url)` (a code span or fence is fine). needs: whose move it is now (the list is described below). due: YYYY-MM-DD UTC, set only from a real deadline (the owner's word, an outside date, or a date a dependency fixes), otherwise left empty: a made-up date reads to the owner as their own deadline (to expect something back by a date, use a wake). ask: the line a needs=decision item carries, written so the owner can decide from it alone and refreshed whenever the question moves, one line of at most 240 characters, "Decide: <what to decide> · Recommend: <your recommendation> · Stakes: <what happens either way> · By: <a date in words such as Mon Jun 8th 2099, or no date>"; example: ask="Decide: whether to approve the sample schema · Recommend: Approve · Stakes: waiting a week delays the demo · By: Mon Jun 8th 2099", options=[{"label": "Approve", "line": "Approve the schema", "recommended": true}, {"label": "Decline", "line": "Wait a week", "recommended": false}]. An ask that only confirms the owner's own action is refused ("have you done X?", a bare "is it done?", or a Decide part that names the action of his own `the owner:` next lines, such as "Decide: install the apps and delete the test repo?"): use step="<his action>" instead (on a create, set it by update after); a real choice between alternatives, a judgement ("have you decided …", "does it work for you?") and an Approve/Decline go-ahead stay decisions. One decision per item: an ask that packs several decisions, or points at choices by a number or letter code the item does not spell out (“choices 2-3”, “2b”), is refused. Split it into one item per decision and write each option out in words in the ask or the description, so that the owner can decide from the item page alone. A decision to change wording quotes the current and the proposed text, labeled before and after, in the description or the options' lines. A needs=decision item whose description or next links a mockup (a https://claude.ai/artifact/… page, or a /mockup/<n> page of the fleet tool's web UI (host set in the instance config)) puts [mockup](<that link>) in the ask's Decide part too, or the write is refused: the home row and the item page show it as Mockup ↗ beside the question. A mockup link goes in the ask only, never in an option: an option label or line holding a markdown link or an http(s) URL is refused. A command for the owner to run, or a paste, belongs on the item: in next when it is short (a code span), otherwise on the project page, with next linking to it. options: when the decision is a pick between alternatives, list them, each on one line, options=[{"label": "<a short name>", "line": "<one sentence, at most 160 characters>", "recommended": true}, {"label": …, "line": …, "recommended": false}, …] (2–6 entries, exactly one recommended); the ask's Recommend names the recommended one's label. The server refuses a needs=decision item whose ask or description names alternatives while it lists none: words such as "which of the two", "pick one", "x, y or z", "x vs y", "Option A", and labeled choices in the Decide part ("A or B", "A (…) or B (…)", "A: … or B: …"); put each alternative in as one option, or the page draws only Yes / No for it. A needs=decision item with no options whose Decide part opens with what, which, how, who, when, where or why is refused (create; an update that sets the ask or options or puts it on his call), since Yes / No cannot answer it: list its answers as options or reword it as a yes/no ("Decide: whether to …"). The same goes for a needs=decision item with no options whose Recommend part is not a yes or a no (it names a person, a topic, a date, whatever the Decide part's wording or language), since the page draws only Yes / No under it: put the choices as options, or make it a yes/no question with a Recommend of yes or no. Name who acts in every option label and line (the owner, a session's name, a role), never "I", "you", "we", "us" or "me"; the ask line likewise never says "I", "you" or "me" (the reply notes one; write "Pat unpublishes", not "I unpublish"). A yes/no decision lists two options, "Approve" and "Decline" (the one you recommend marked recommended: true), so the owner gets one-click buttons. options="none" clears them (refused while the ask is an open question). Write the project page first, then the board: a page write up to five minutes before the change counts. next replaces only your own lines: every line of next remembers the session whose update wrote it (the sender, or the item's creator when the call names none; not the name the line starts with). next=<lines> takes the place of the lines you wrote before, where the first of them stood (at the end when you had none) and leaves every other session's lines where they are; an open step of yours that the new next leaves out must be marked in the same update, done=[n] or dropped=[n] (a line reworded in next alone is a new step: mark the old one and write the new text, or pass reword). next="none" removes only your own lines; clear_next=true wipes every line, whoever wrote it, and with next given the wipe comes first and your lines are then set. A line of yours that another session's open line already reads the same is not added a second time. A close clears next whoever wrote it. ask="none" clears it (so does clear_ask=true). A write that leaves an ask standing on an item you move or wrote ends with a one-line reminder to withdraw the ask if it is wrong or moot; a write that sets an ask shows the owner's comments and notes since the item's last ask, so one that already answers it is seen before you ask again. His note on a step that only says he did it ("ran it"; "run it" is a request and ticks nothing) ticks the step, and one in which he says he will do it later ("I'll do it tomorrow evening") holds the item until then; any other note (a question, a negation, a deadline, more than that) goes to the session to judge. The ask's mockup rule above also holds on an update that sets the ask, description, next, needs or options or puts the item on needs=decision. options=[] (or "none", or clear_options=true) clears the options, which need no recommended one then (refused while the ask is an open question; a non-empty list still takes 2 to 6 entries, exactly one recommended). When the owner answers by picking an option, the server clears the ask and the options itself and keeps his answer with the option's label and line. A client whose tool has no ask parameter refreshes the ask by writing the new line, in the ask's form, as the first line of next. When this work settles or changes a premise of another open item, update that one too, in the same turn. item_id: board#N; a bare number N is read as board#N, except in an update that closes the item. wake (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM for a time of day, UTC; a full ISO time with seconds or a UTC offset is converted to that minute in UTC, and the reply says so) alone is a wait: the item waits until that date, listed as waiting, and at that moment the server tells its mover and the sessions in its needs once and drops the date; in an update that hands the item to another session the date is no wait but the hand-off's backstop, and the item stays active (unless the item carries hold, wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait). Work moving in real time is not parked. A doing item whose wake is over an hour away and whose every open step waits for a later date ("after Mar 2", "until Mar 2"; a deadline such as "by Mar 2" or "due Mar 2" is no wait) is listed as waiting, and the audit asks why the step cannot run now. A front agent's own wake or until date (no hold) on an alive item another session moves is refused (the result lands through stackshot when the mover closes the item or hands it back to you; watch_reason=<why no push reaches you> lets a real exception through; a park's wake with hold=true is a wait of its own and stays allowed). On hold = an open item parked until its next move is due: hold=true, always passed explicitly, with what it waits for; with a wake the server releases it at that moment, tells the sessions in its needs (else its mover; refresh the ask then) and returns it to the lane its needs give it. Meanwhile it reads as parked (a waiting state), not as work moving on agent; needs and due stay as they are. An item whose needs hold decision is never on hold: a write to one drops its hold (its date stays, and no date parks an item on his call). the owner parks on his word. A hold always names what it waits for: the owner's words, the items that must close first (after), a notice from an anchor scoped to the item, a pane recycle (recycle=true), or the end of a window the work itself needs; an unconditional or indefinite park is refused. Work moving in real time stays on agent however long it takes (a build, tests, a review, a release, a run in progress): do not park it. A session parks its own item when the work itself needs a wait-and-see window (a soak, a log or data collection window, a trial week, a timer it started): hold=true, until=<when the window ends>, wait_basis="<what the window collects> ends <YYYY-MM-DD>" (update(item_id="board#N", sender="my-x", hold=true, until="<YYYY-MM-DD, a future day>", wait_basis="error-log soak ends <that day, YYYY-MM-DD>")). A session does not park to defer work it could do now: an item not on hold is one its mover can move now, so work it in your next free turn. A wake without hold whose next says the work waits for that wake's day within a line ("collect logs until <that day>, then review") gets a note on the reply, never a refusal: the wake is stored, the item stays on agent, the note gives the park form above. When your write sets or keeps a wake with no hold over an hour ahead, you are the item's mover and every open step opens with a time at the wake's hour or day ("at 03:00", "on <that day>", "after <that day>", "tomorrow at 9"), the server parks it itself: on hold, wait_basis from your wait_reason; the reply says `(parked: …)`; to work a step now, write it as the action and pass clear_hold=true: the server then leaves that wake alone. Steps started by an outside event ("when the next release lands") get a note instead: park with hold=true, wake, wait_basis, wait_reason (needs=external for a named outside party's reply). Neither applies to an action to take now, another party's step in flight, or an item not on agent (on hold, waiting on the owner's decision or an open after item, needs=external, outside, verifying, blocked). An item that waits on another item is not parked but names it: after=["board#N"]. Nor is one that waits on the owner: needs=decision with its ask, or after=<the item that carries the ask>. When an item's work moves to another project's session, hand the item over in the same turn: mover = that project's user-facing agent (or the background agent doing the work), project = its page. The creator is not moved with it. owner, the old name of mover, is accepted for a few more days with a note in the reply and then refused: say mover. sender = your own session (name or cse_… id) when you edit an item you are not the mover of (a session named in needs always passes sender=<itself>): the page update the edit owes is then yours, not the mover's (a create, a complete, or an update to description, next, needs, status, due, after, or the hold and its wake owes one). While the GitHub mirror is on, sender is required on every update, confirm and complete, the mover's own included. Pass clear_needs=true (or needs="none") to remove the needs badge, clear_check=true (or check="none") to remove the done check, clear_due=true (or due="none") to remove a date that no longer holds (a postponement with no new date). priority: p1 | p2 | p3, shown but not sorted. project re-files the item under another page (projects/<slug> or infra/<slug>; pass the page `(filed on X)` names, never the shown top-level key). A state change also confirms the item (it reads fresh again); the confirm tool says it is still true without changing it. recycle=true: the item's work waits for the panes to be relaunched (a connector re-login, a settings, hook or plugin change, a CLI update; not a change to a connector's tools, which claude.ai refreshes on its own within about a day); set it only once the change it waits for is installed (merged and deployed, or provisioned), never before: an early flag recycles the panes too soon, for nothing (a flag set before the provision recycled the box too early). Set it on the item the change serves: a recycle is never an item of its own (create refuses one), and for a change no item covers, leave it for the next recycle (no idle-recycle command is configured); the fleet tool runs a flagged recycle itself, the board shows one "Pane recycle pending for … (the fleet tool runs it)" status line while an open item not on hold carries it, and when the fleet tool reports the recycle done the server clears it and tells you to re-read the item and resume. clear_recycle=true takes it off by hand. work: the status of your open step, one line per call: work={"text": "PR 83 up", "state": "in progress"}, a few words (at most 40 characters; the details stay on the project page). A step is a stage of the work ("stage 11: auth and who"), not a status: what changes while it is under way goes in this status, which replaces the status of your first open step in place, so a night of updates is one line on the step, not one line each. state is in progress (the default) or done; done also ticks the step, as done=[n] does. With no open step of yours the call makes one from the text; {"remove": true} clears the status. Written by the mover or a session named in needs; it changes no needs, owes no page and, unless it ticks or makes a step, leaves the state clock and the confirm alone. A project builder's step with a status in progress (changed within 90 minutes) tells the stall pass and the balancer that a build subagent is running on the item, so the item is not handed on meanwhile; a status left in progress stops hiding the item after that, and a status sent again unchanged keeps its old time, so a long job changes the words or writes to the item; mark the step done when the subagent ends. A question the owner asks on an item (in his answer or a comment on it) is answered by the mover on the item itself: rewrite the description, and the options where it is a pick, the description saying it answers his question. His question is never posted with said and never taken as his call; only his conclusions are. needs: whose move it is now, a list: "decision" (the owner's: decide, judge, review, give the go-ahead), "external" (someone outside, named in next) and session names (a background agent of any project, or the item's one mover; a user-facing agent that is not the mover is refused: its part becomes its own item, linked with after=), e.g. needs=["decision", "my-engineer"] or one comma-separated string. An item has one mover: a session named that is not a background agent of the item's project counts as a mover, and two of them, or decision beside one, are refused (name the one who moves it now, and who takes it after his answer in then=); a background agent of this project never counts as a second mover; empty means the item's mover (mover=, else the project's builder, else its -main agent) moves it. The lane follows the first of decision, external, a session (your call · on others · on agent). A session named is told when added, is asked about the item at each turn end and hears its wake, recycle and after notices; it passes sender=<its name> on its writes, so that they reach the mover as another session's. needs= replaces the whole list (name again what should stay); needs="none" or clear_needs=true empties it. decision vs your-step: needs=decision is the owner's call, a choice between options; a thing that is the owner's own to do is step=<his action> (update; a create has no step), and the board ticks it when he says it is done, so an ask that only asks whether he has done it is refused. agent=<session> is the older form: it makes that session the one named in needs (the decision and external entries stay); agent="none" takes the sessions out. observers: sessions that hear only a close or a reopen; observers="none" clears. after: items of any project that must close first (after=["board#N"]); while one is open the item counts as waiting without a hold, and when the last one closes it wakes and the sessions in its needs (else its mover) are told; a dropped one releases it too, a superseded one is followed to its replacement; a loop is refused; after="none" clears. after is for a real dependency (this item needs that one's output), never for the order a builder takes its items in. A hold (hold=true) names what it waits for (a wake, after items, a notice from an anchor scoped to the item, a recycle, or a wait_basis window the work itself needs); one with none is refused. A wake (or until) without hold=true is a wait: the item is listed as waiting until that date (a wake past the cap takes a wait_basis); in an update that hands the item to another session it is only the hand-off's backstop and the item stays active (unless the item carries hold, wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait). An item waiting on the owner is never on hold: it carries needs=decision with its ask, or after=<the item that carries the ask>. needs names only who can move now. An item that waits on the owner and on a session at once: where his answer could change with the session's work, or its work with his answer, the session goes first and adds decision when it is done (or the decision is its own item, linked with after=); decision sits beside this project's background agents only when the two are independent (beside any other session it is refused), and when unsure, in sequence. When decision leaves needs (he has decided), the sessions still named are told at once; a session whose work changes the question rewrites the ask. The server never hands an item to a front agent on its own motion: when the item is back with its front agent mover alone, the project's builder is told instead. check: what closes this item once the work handed to another session is done, a check the server runs itself every minute and, when it passes, closes the item with outcome done and a reason naming the check: pr_merged <owner>/<repo>#<n> (the pull request is merged), item_closed <id> (that board item is completed), lane <session> <lane> (the fleet tool's lane record puts that pane on that lane; only where one is configured), unit_active <unit>.service (the systemd user unit is active on the server box); nothing else, never a command. A check the server cannot read (GitHub down, a unit not found) never closes. A release of a pull request of the board's own repository needs no check: once main's full run passed on its merge and that merge is in the last-good commit and the live checkout, the server ticks a step that says it releases that PR (`release PR #<n>`, `release #<n>`, or `release` before the PR's URL; the step events, below, say what counts), only on an item anchored to that PR or naming its URL. An item whose only open steps are that release is completed, outcome done; on an item with any other open step the release step is ticked done and the mover told once. A step that only mentions the PR (investigate, review, verify) is never ticked and never closes the item. An item on hold, or whose needs name his decision or a session other than its mover, is left alone; a check that passes while the item waits on his decision does not close it until the decision is cleared. An update whose next hands the work to another session (a line of next in the form `<session>: <action>`, a list marker before the name at most: any session but the item's mover and you, not one already in needs; a name elsewhere, in a slug, a link or a sentence, hands nothing over) is refused unless the item carries a check or a wake (or until), the hand-off's backstop: with a hand-off the date is no wait (unless the item carries hold, wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait), the item stays active in the new mover's lane; a write that leaves an existing hand-off as it was is not asked again. Right: update(item_id="board#N", sender="my-x", next="other-x: build the export", check="pr_merged acme/widgets#12"). A front agent is the exception: its hand-off needs neither (a check stays allowed to anyone), because a front agent does not watch handed-off work itself: the result lands through stackshot when the mover closes the item or hands it back to you, so a front agent's own wake or until date (no hold) on an alive item another session moves is refused (a done check, a park with its wake and ask_by stay allowed). To watch anyway, pass watch_reason=<why no push reaches you> (at least 15 characters) on update, in the same call; it is recorded on the item. check="none" clears it; a check alone owes no page. A check does not set the item's due time. check="" changes nothing, and a new check passed replaces the old one. Parameter contact (a filing field: it moves no state clock, changes no mover and sends no notice; get shows it as `contact:`): the front agent that the owner talks to about the item; the parameter says how it is set and when it falls to the project's -main agent. The item model (design: docs/design): an item is dead (closed), alive (someone in the perimeter is working: one mover) or waiting (nothing happens until something outside arrives). mover is how an item says whose move it is (the sender of a create is recorded as its creator). Optional fields, stored as given (each parameter says how it is set): goal=<the end-state in one sentence, what the owner would ask "is it done?" about>; mover=<who moves an alive item now: the owner, a session name or the project's background agent; a front agent (a session the owner talks to) only by itself: a create or update from another session that sets mover to one gets the project's builder instead, and the reply and History say so (send the same mover again to keep it; with no builder it is refused)>; then=<who takes it after the owner's answer or step; then=<front agent> from another session gets the builder the same way>; wait_kind=time | anchor | item | relay | event; wait_anchor=<url of the anchor an anchor wait watches>, which must be on the project's anchors list first (add it with the anchors tool, scoped to this item), else the write is refused; wait_event=<what you expect there (an anchor wait), or the party or event the owner relays (a relay wait), or the fleet event an event wait watches: pr_released <owner/repo#n> | pr_merged <owner/repo#n> | recycle [<machine>] | fleet_op <verb | any | many> [<machine>] | job_run <name> | box_online <machine>>; ask_by=YYYY-MM-DD (a relay wait's end day; an event, item or anchor wait's backstop day, as a wake is); post_wake_mover=<who moves it when the wait ends; a front agent only by itself, as for mover>. An event wait is how an item whose mover waits in the background for something the fleet does says so: update(wait_kind="event", wait_event="pr_released <n>" (this repository's pull request number), ask_by=<the day it comes back anyway, required>, post_wake_mover=<who takes it then>). Live for now: pr_released, pr_merged, box_online, recycle, and every fleet_op form (any verb, any, many); a job_run wait turns only on its backstop day. box_online <machine> waits for a machine to be online (its puller checking in, within the minutes the server counts as online): the server reads it itself and the item turns within a minute or two of the machine's return, so an item waiting on a date for an offline machine says wait_event="box_online <machine>" with that date as ask_by instead; the machine must be one the fleet knows (an unknown name is refused with the known ones). The backstop must be after now, and a day (ask_by=YYYY-MM-DD) falls due at 00:00 of that day in the instance timezone, so today's date is already past: give tomorrow at the earliest, or a wake time later today. A wait for something that has already happened (a PR already merged or live, a machine already online) is refused; a recycle wait never asks for a recycle (it waits for the next one). A step of his, or needs holding decision, makes him the mover: a write that names a session as mover beside it is refused (leave mover out, or mover=the owner, and put the session in then). The mirror is refused too: a write that leaves an open item with mover=the owner but in none of his states, so it has no step and no ask, is refused: pass step=<one line>, or needs=["decision"] with ask=…, or give the item to a session (mover=<session>) and write his part in a next line that starts `the owner:`. A waiting item, a close, a rename, a priority or project write and a re-bullet are not judged by it. A wait that replaces his state drops the mover and keeps then as the post-wake mover. "none" clears a field; clear_goal, clear_mover and clear_then clear theirs, clear_wait the wait's five (wait_kind, wait_anchor, wait_event, ask_by, post_wake_mover). A close drops the mover and the wait and keeps the goal. The wait ends by itself when its kind's event comes: a time at its wake; an item when the last `after` item closes; an anchor when the anchor watcher's notice for wait_anchor reaches the server, and any new notice at the anchor that reaches the server and passes the project's keeper wakes the item; an event when the server is told of it; a relay on its ask_by day, when it comes to the owner as a question (arrived / not yet, ask again on a date / drop); a date beside it is its backstop. The item then turns alive with its post_wake_mover. A moved ask_by or wake resets the backstop. next is a checklist: each line of next is a step, and the item keeps every step in the order it was written, open, done or dropped; next holds the open steps. A step of yours leaves next only by being marked in the same update: done=[…] when the work was finished, dropped=[…] when it is no longer wanted, each entry a step's 1-based position in the checklist (marked steps count; get lists the steps under `checklist:` with their positions) or the exact text of its first line. An update that replaces or removes (next="none") your own lines of next and leaves one of them out without marking it is refused, naming the step, its position and the call to retry with (done=[n], dropped=[n] or reword={n: "<new text>"}); another session's lines are never touched by your next. Parameter reword (map, step position or first-line text → new text, e.g. reword={3: "my-x: new words"}) gives an open step of yours new words: it keeps its number, place and open state, and next lists the new text (leave next out and the line is changed for you); a line reworded in next alone is a new step, and the old one is refused unmarked. A reword is the same action in other words, never the old text with words added (progress goes on the project page). Refused: a step of another session or of his, one that is done or dropped, or also in done or dropped, a text of several steps or one another open step reads; a different action is a new line of next. done and dropped mark any open step, whoever wrote it, and the marked line leaves next, except a step of his (a line opening with his name) while the item asks him: that one is ticked when he answers, and done on it is refused (dropped on it is undone while the item still asks him). The server makes his step itself: when an item asks him for a decision (needs=decision with an ask) or for a step (your-step), it adds the open step `<his name>: <what to decide>` at the end of the checklist (a line you wrote that says the same is adopted, never a second beside it), shows his answer on the step when he gives it, and drops the step when you withdraw the ask or the step; a step he already answered stays done. clear_next=true is a deliberate wipe: every line it removes becomes a dropped step, by you. A marked step stays on the page with who marked it and when; History says `step done: …` or `step dropped: …`. done or dropped alone, with no next, takes the step out of next; when two open steps read the same, the position names the one marked. A step written again after it was marked is a new step. the owner's word that his step is done checks every open step of his, each next line that starts `the owner:`; a note he sends ticks the step the server made and leaves the lines you wrote open, and the session that takes the item marks them done when it judges the step finished. A step can name the event that finishes it, and the server then ticks it done when the event happens: a pull request merged (pr_merged), or released, i.e. merged and live (pr_released: this repository's with main's tests passed, or a configured repository's). A step that is only `release PR #<n>`, `release #<n>` or `release <URL>` (or the same with `merge`), with at most a short parenthetical (`(in its turn)`) and a closing full stop, is ticked when that pull request is released, on an item anchored to the PR or naming its URL. Anything else after the phrase (`and verify the pages`, `, restart x`, ` then …`) is a follow-up: the step stays open and its mover is told once; a condition (`once #<n> is released, …`, `when PR #<n> is merged, …`, `release it after #<n>`) is never ticked either, and its mover is told once it is met. A negated phrase (`do not release PR #<n>`), a step that only mentions the PR (review, verify, investigate), another repository's #<n> without its URL, and a step of his never match. step_proof=[{"step": <position or the step's exact first line>, "proof": "pr_merged <owner>/<repo>#<n>" | "pr_released <owner>/<repo>#<n>"}] states the proof outright, whatever the step's words say (a bare #<n> is this repository's, a URL works too; "proof": "none" clears one step's proof, step_proof="none" every one; the step must be open). When the event arrives the server marks the step done and tells its mover the next open step once; with no open step left the item closes, outcome done. A pull request closed without a merge ticks nothing. A done step whose next open step names another session makes that session the mover and tells it. A step that delivers a PR (`release`, `merge`) and is followed by another session's step must be only that phrase or carry step_proof, or the write is refused. draft: the text exactly as it is to be posted, sent or pasted somewhere else by the person whose step it is (a channel message, an email, a reply), as many lines as it has, stored and shown as written (no bullets, no line limit; at most 20000 characters). His item page draws it under the step as a block with a Copy button; a close drops it, and so does his Done or Send note on the step. A next line that starts with his name (`the owner:`) and asks him to run something gets the command check, on create and update, whatever the item's state, for the lines the call sets (the cue and the `! ` rule are under next above): a command outside backticks is refused as `next line: …`; a line that only mentions a command is not checked. A bare command with a flag, path or quoted argument, written outside backticks or a fence after a run cue or a place phrase ("In a terminal: ls -la"), is a command too: the step carries none, and a next line gets it in backticks so the board shows a copy box. A write that leaves an item for him to move (him as mover, in his step, or with his decision in needs) is refused when its description adds a numbered line (`1.`, `2)`) or a `! ` line outside a fenced block: the description is the background, never steps. A write that leaves an item in your-step for him is refused, in one line naming the field, when the description holds a shell command (move it to a next line that starts `the owner:`; a description write is judged only on the commands it adds or changes, and a fence there counts only when tagged sh, bash, shell, powershell, pwsh or console, and each command line of a tagged fence is judged; an untagged fence holds pasted output), or when the step points elsewhere ("see the description", "see below", or a phrase of [keywords.step_commands] pointer_patterns); a step that names his Next line passes. The check passes the write when the model is unavailable or slow. A note, never a refusal. A wait is one stored date, until, with wait_kind beside it when it stands on more than the date. A wait_kind with no date is never refused: the server takes a date from the item's words, else a suggested one, else tomorrow, and says which. Every open item has a mover (the one party whose move it is now: a session, the owner, an outside party, or the item it waits `after`). An open item waits on its real dates only (wake, due, ask by): no expected time is derived for any item, and a parked item is held until its wake or its blocker closes, with no stale mark. Three wakes take it: a hold's wake (it parks the item, which reads as waiting, not on agent, until the wake), a stored verifying item's wake, and a wake past the cap (it lifts the cap for that wake alone; clear_wait_basis=true drops it). A bare date within the cap (until, or its old name wake) is a wait on its own, and a basis for it is refused as not needed unless the item is on hold (hold=true) or verifying; a date no longer leaves the item active as a reminder (outside a hand-off's backstop): set no date to keep an item moving. A hold with a wake and no basis, where the item's own next or its description says the work waits for that wake's day ("collect the logs until 2099-03-02, then review"), takes that line as its wait_basis (the reply says so); a basis needs a wake date (a hold with no date is refused) and names the date it waits for as YYYY-MM-DD on or after the wake day. A wait that can no longer end (a check whose pull request was closed unmerged) fails at once and tells the item's mover. clear_wait=true is how an update drops a stored wait (wait_kind and its fields); wait_anchor or wait_event of none and clear_wait_basis do not. An update that newly adds needs=decision to an item that stores a wait is refused unless it also passes clear_wait=true: the wait would otherwise win and get would list a model conflict. clear_after=true clears the after list, as after=[] or after="none" do; some clients drop an empty list, so the flag always arrives. A write that clears a wait while an open next line still defers on what it cleared in words goes through, and its reply carries one line per stale next line (`(note: next line N still waits on board#X, whose wait was just cleared: reword it)`): reword or drop those lines in the same turn. An item stores alive or waiting directly; there is no state to set, and these are not parameters of this tool or of create: a call that passes state, clear_state, party, chase, end, proof or chase_note is refused with what to pass instead. Whose move it is goes in mover; the owner's call is needs=["decision"] with an ask; his own step is step=<one line, no command, of the single thing only the owner does; what he runs goes in a next line that starts `the owner:`> (the board ticks it when he says it is done; never ask him "have you done it?" as a decision); a wait on another item is after=["board#N"] (supplies=<one line: what that item's output gives this one> says what it takes from it); a park is hold=true with a wake and either his recorded words for it (cap_ok) or a wait_basis (the end of a window the work itself needs, or a wake past the cap); a wait on someone outside is wait_kind="relay" with wait_event=<who>, ask_by=<the day to chase>, post_wake_mover and needs=["external"]. Work in hand needs next and its mover, carries no expected time (the item shows how long it has run), and expected_by and expected_reason, which older calls pass, are accepted and not kept (the reply says so). Work in hand is not a wait: a wait (a date, a timer, another release, someone else's step) is parked in the turn it starts, with update(hold=true, until="YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", wait_basis="<what it waits for, with its date YYYY-MM-DD>"), update(after=["board#N"]) for another item, or the relay wait above for someone outside (a write that leaves an item with wait wording in its next, such as overnight, in the morning, once the run finishes, gets a note saying to park it). No clock renewal without progress: a write that moves a wake or ask_by to a later time while the item's reason (description, wait_basis text) and its open steps are as they were is refused (a wait_reason does not count: it is not stored); in the same write mark a step done or dropped, write the next step or state the new reason (or send the owner's own words in said), or change what the wait stands on to a shape the item never held (wait_kind, wait_event, wait_anchor, after: a flip back to an earlier one does not count; such a shape change alone lets a clock push through twice in a row and the third is refused, until a step, the reason, his new words or a hand-off resets the count); or, if the item now waits, park it (hold=true, wake, wait_basis) or use the event-wait form (wait_kind="event", wait_event, ask_by, post_wake_mover). Setting a clock for the first time, pulling one in, clearing it and handing the item to another session are not renewals. On a parked item give a new wait_basis; an item on his decision cannot be held. Take a wake from the real schedule of the wait (a timer, a watch tick, a catch-up run), or check it live; never a guessed round time. step=<one line> sets the item in his step and makes him the mover (then, or the agent that had it, takes it after his Done); step="none" withdraws it; supplies=<one line: what the item it waits after gives this one>, with after=["board#N"], sets the item blocked on that item. Each is refused without what it needs, with what to add; a close drops both. Checks: a next that opens with the owner: or you: under an agent's state is noted; the third bare re-park in a row is refused; a next may be marked stale; needs=decision again within 60 min of his answer is refused unless the ask changed.

after.description: Items this one waits on: after=["board#N"], with ask_by=<YYYY-MM-DD> as the day it comes back if they are still open. The wait ends when they close.

ask.description: The one line a needs=decision item carries, at most 240 characters: ask="Decide: whether to approve the sample schema · Recommend: Approve · Stakes: waiting a week delays the demo · By: Mon Jun 8th 2099" (By is a date in words, or no date). A real choice, not "have you done X?"; one decision per ask. With no options listed the Recommend is a yes or a no. Name who acts (a person or a session name) in every option, never I, you, we, us or me; the ask line never says I, you or me. "none" or clear_ask=true withdraws it.

ask_by.description: The old name of until, accepted for now: the day a wait on another item, a relay or an event comes back to someone if it has not ended, YYYY-MM-DD, tomorrow at the earliest: ask_by="2099-03-02". Moving it later with nothing else changed is refused (see wake).

check.description: What closes the item once work handed to another session is done; the server runs it every minute: check="pr_merged acme/widgets#12" (also item_closed <item id>, lane <session> <lane>, unit_active <unit>.service). A next line that hands the item to a session other than its mover and you needs a check or, instead, a date (wake or until) as the hand-off's backstop: with a hand-off the date is no wait (unless the item carries hold, wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait), the item stays active in the new mover's lane and the hand-off is recorded; a front agent needs neither. check="none" clears it.

clear_rank.description: Retired: refused. Ranks are retired; a call that carries this is refused.

contact.description: The item's contact: the front agent (a user-facing agent) that the owner talks to about it, by its name. Leave it out and the contact is the creator when that is a front agent, else the project's -main agent. A background agent that creates an item may name one of the project's front agents here; any other name is refused, and the refusal lists the project's front agents with their mandates. On an update it changes the contact with the same check; an update that re-files the item under another project (project=) makes that project's -main agent the contact, unless contact is passed too, the contact is a front agent of that project as well, or the contact is the item's creator and a front agent of any project (it stays). The same fall to the -main agent happens when the contact retires.

description.description: The item's background as short `- ` bullets, at most 8 lines of 120 characters, live state only (never steps or commands): description="- Goal: the export finishes in under a minute\n- Problem: the nightly run takes 9 minutes". The first bullet opens `Goal:` (case-sensitive), a symptom or cause goes in a later `Problem:` bullet, the owner's words go in a bullet such as `- the owner: …`, and parallel bullets go under one parent bullet, indented two spaces.

done.description: Open steps of the checklist you finished: positions (1-based, marked steps count) or the exact first line, e.g. done=[1] or done=[1, "my-x: open the PR"]. A step of yours that next leaves out must be in done or dropped.

dropped.description: Open steps that are no longer wanted, named like done: dropped=[2]. A different action is a new line of next, not a reword.

hold.description: The old way to wait on a date, accepted for now (stored as until). True parks the item until its wake, for a window the work itself needs: hold=true, until="<last day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD>", wait_basis="soak ends <that day>". It reads as waiting, not on agent; clear_hold=true ends it.

mover.description: Who moves the item now: the owner, a session name or id, or the project's background agent. A front agent (a session the owner talks to) only by itself: it gets no hand-off notice, so a create or update from another session that sets mover=<front agent> gets the project's builder instead (the reply and History say so; send mover=<front agent> again and it is kept as sent; with no builder it is refused unless sender and target are both front agents of the item's project); message the front agent for a check or an answer only it can give. On an update that sets no needs, the session needs names for the mover it replaces is swapped for the new one.

next.description: Your lines of the checklist, one step per line, each opening with who takes it, then a space: next="my-x: open the PR" (a label such as `Status:` names no one). It replaces only your own lines; a line of yours it leaves out must be marked in done or dropped (or reword) in the same call. An item that stays open keeps one open step, a held one the step its wake leads to. Never reword an open step to add progress. next="none" removes your open lines; an empty next is next not passed.

options.description: The alternatives of a decision, one per line: options=[{"label": "Approve", "line": "Approve the schema", "recommended": true}, {"label": "Decline", "line": "Wait a week", "recommended": false}] (2-6 entries, exactly one recommended, each line at most 160 characters). A yes/no decision lists Approve and Decline. Name who acts in every option, label and line: a person or a session name, never I, you, we, us or me.

outcome.description: How a close ended: done | dropped (won't do, no longer needed, or can't) | superseded (replaced by another item: reworded, merged or split; send superseded_by=<the replacing item's id>). Passed on update with status=completed, or on complete: outcome="done", reason="Export shipped in PR 12", outcome_text="- PR 12 merged"; all three are required.

outcome_text.description: A close's summary: how the item ended, as short `- ` bullets (at most 8 lines of 120 characters), stored in the item's Outcome field. A close does not change the item's description. Goes with a close only.

post_wake_mover.description: Who moves the item when its wait ends (it becomes the mover then): the owner, a session name or id, or the project's background agent. A front agent only by itself: a create or update from another session that sets post_wake_mover=<front agent> gets the project's builder instead, as for mover.

project.description: Re-files the item under this page, as `(filed on X)` shows it, never the shown top-level key.

rank.description: Retired: refused. Ranks are retired; a call that carries this is refused.

reason.description: One line, at most 120 characters (longer is refused): the end state reached and why. Goes with outcome on a close.

reword.description: New words for open steps of your own next: a mapping from a step (1-based position, or the exact text of its first line, as done takes them) to its new text, e.g. {"3": "my-x: wait for the new build"}; the step keeps its number and stays open, and the new text is one step that opens with who takes it (the rules are under Parameter reword in the description).

said.description: A list of entries, two kinds. (1) His own words {tag: Acked-by (his decision) | Suggested-by (his idea or request) | Reported-by (a problem he reported), quote: his words verbatim, msg: the uuid of his message's transcript entry, session: the session that heard him (default: you)}; it is checked against that transcript and the write is refused when it does not match. Post his conclusions, never his questions. (2) Proof he did a step {kind: "acted", quote, msg, session} with no tag: a message he sends while your session is working is an attachment entry (type queued_command, origin human): msg is that entry's uuid, quote a piece of its attachment.prompt verbatim; any other entry is refused. It is stored as Done-by, kind acted, and counts only as proof of steps he did within 24 hours after its date, never as his words or his decision.

step_proof.description: The event that finishes a step, so the server ticks it: [{step: its 1-based position or exact first line, proof: pr_merged|pr_released <owner>/<repo>#<n> (or none to clear that step's)}], or the string none to clear them all; the step must be open and not the owner's own.

then.description: Who takes the item after the owner's answer or step (it becomes the mover then): a session name or id, or the project's background agent. A front agent only by itself: a create or update from another session that sets then=<front agent> gets the project's builder instead, as for mover.

until.description: The one date a wait ends on, in the future: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM, in the board timezone (a relay or event wait takes the day alone, YYYY-MM-DD: its ask-by day). An item with an until is waiting (outside a hand-off: in an update that hands the item to another session the date parks nothing, it is the hand-off's backstop and the item stays active in the new mover's lane (unless the item carries hold, wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait)); wait_kind goes only beside it (none: it waits on the date alone). until="none" drops it. It replaces wake, ask_by and hold with a wake, still accepted for now. Moving it later with nothing else changed is refused, as for wake.

wait_basis.description: The reason a time wait's wake carries, one line that names its date: wait_basis="soak ends <that day, YYYY-MM-DD>" (YYYY-MM-DD, on or after the wake day; a wake with no date is refused). Three wakes take it, each basis bound to the wake it was given for: a hold's wake (the park), a verifying item's wake, and a wake more than 7 days out (it lifts the cap for that wake alone, up to 365 days: a wake further out is refused whatever the basis). A hold with a wake and no basis takes the line of next or the description that says what the work waits for.

wait_event.description: The event the wait expects. An anchor wait: what you expect at the anchor, which the post-wake mover checks, since any new notice there that reaches the server and passes the project's keeper wakes the item; a wait_event naming a merge, close, landing or completion is not woken by a routine push or CI line on the fleet's own PR (only by one that says merged or closed). A relay wait: the party or event the owner relays. An event wait: the fleet event, one of pr_released <owner/repo#n> | pr_merged <owner/repo#n> | recycle [<machine>] | fleet_op <verb | any | many> [<machine>] | job_run <name> | box_online <machine> (live today: pr_released, pr_merged, box_online, recycle and every fleet_op form; job_run turns only on the backstop day; box_online <machine> ends when that machine is online and is refused while it already is, or for a machine the fleet does not know; an item waiting on a date for an offline machine says wait_event="box_online <machine>" with that date as ask_by instead). "none" clears it.

wait_kind.description: What a waiting item waits on: time | anchor | item | relay | event. A time wait is its wake; an item wait its after; an anchor wait its wait_anchor (on the project's anchors list first: add it with the anchors tool) and wait_event (a wake is the backstop); a relay wait its wait_event and ask_by; an event wait its wait_event (a fleet event) and a backstop day (ask_by or a wake). An anchor wait wakes the item on any new notice at its anchor that reaches the server and passes the project's keeper, not only on the awaited event, so it fits something quiet apart from that event (a PR, a thread, a file) and not a busy channel or DM; for a busy channel use a relay wait (it is put to someone on a day) or a time wait (check back on a date). "none" clears it.

wait_reason.description: What the step waits on that is not available now (a reply, a build or test still running, a window the work needs, a resource that is down), at least 15 characters. Required when this write sets a wake, or a line of your own next dated later than today, on an item you move: without it the write is refused, and a model may refuse it when the step could be done now. Not stored on the item. A park (hold=true with wait_basis), a wait on another item (after) and needs decision or external need none. A date after by, due or before is a deadline, not a wait.

wake.description: The old name of until, accepted for now: when the item wakes, in the future: YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM for a time of day, in the board timezone. Alone it is a wait: the item waits until that date (outside a hand-off: in an update that hands the item to another session the date parks nothing, it is the hand-off's backstop (unless the item carries hold, wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait)). A window the work needs: wake="<last day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD>", wait_basis="soak ends <that day>". A wait on your own item also needs wait_reason (at least 15 characters); a wait with wait_basis needs none, and a wake more than 7 days out needs a wait_basis. Moving a wake (or ask_by) later with the item otherwise as it was is refused: in the same write mark a step done or dropped, write the next step or a new reason, or change what the wait stands on (wait_kind, wait_event, wait_anchor, after; a flip back to an earlier one does not count, and a wait_reason does not count).

work.description: The status of your open step, one line per call: {"text": "PR 83 up", "state": "in progress"}. It replaces the status of your first open step in place (the step is the stage, the status says where you are in it; the page keeps one line per step, not one per write). text is at most 40 characters (details go on the project page). state: in progress (the default) | done. state done also ticks the step, as done=[n] does. With no open step of yours, one is made from the text. {"remove": true} clears the status. Keys: text, state, remove. A project builder's step with a status in progress (changed within 90 minutes) tells the stall pass and the balancer that a build subagent is running on the item; a status left in progress stops hiding the item after that, and a status sent again unchanged keeps its old time, so a long job changes the words or marks the step done.
